neighbours.label: the joining word of a fixed parallel saying whose two halves mirror each other (use it or lose it, go big or go home, see no evil, hear no evil), as against an ordinary 'or'/'and' between clauses
fire: The coach told the rookies to put up or shut up before the final.
Her landlord's attitude was simple: like it or lump it.
The sergeant warned the recruits to shape up or ship out.
Money at the casino is easy come, easy go, as my uncle says.
In the jungle it is a case of eat or be eaten.
Monkey see, monkey do, so watch what you say around the kids.
The startup's motto was move fast and break things.
Researchers often feel they must publish or perish.
quiet: The coach told the rookies to sit down or leave the room before the final.
Her landlord's offer was simple: pay in cash or by cheque.
The sergeant told the recruits to wait outside or go to the canteen.
Money at the casino is counted twice, as my uncle says.
In the jungle it is a case of rain or heavy fog.
The children see the teacher and copy the drawing on the board.
The startup's plan was to hire staff and rent an office.
Researchers often write a report or give a talk.
